newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to donate $50 mln U.S. aid money to Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Israel to donate $50 mln U.S. aid money to Jordan.

text.p: Israel will donate $50 million a year from its massive U.S. foreign aid package to aid neighbouring Jordan, an adviser to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday.
"We finalised it on Thursday. Jordan's need for financial aid at this time is palpable, and Israel decided to do its share," Netanyahu's communications adviser David Bar-Illan told Reuters.
"We feel that we are friends, and friends should help each other in time of need," Bar-Illan said.

Israel, which receives $3 billion in U.S. civilian and military aid each year, is the largest recipient of U.S. aid. Egypt, whose $2 billion aid package is second only to Israel's, is considering a similar deal, a U.S. official told Reuters.

The official called the move a way to reward Jordan for remaining in the Middle East "peace camp". Jordan made peace with Israel in 1994 and has gone farther than any other Arab state in normalising ties with the Jewish state.

The move would be the first time the Jewish state agreed to reduce its U.S. assistance. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pledged to the U.S. Congress shortly after taking power one year ago he would work to reduce Israel's dependence on U.S. aid.

Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor told Reuters he would travel to Washington this week to discuss details of the plan with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Jordanian Crown Prince Hassan.
Israel's Haaretz newspaper reported that the Israeli Treasury would return $50 million of its civilian aid back to the United States in 1997 and 1998 to be transferred to Jordan.
Haaretz said that in subsequent years the $50 million could be deducted directly from Israel's aid package.
The newspaper said Israel preferred returning aid to the United States rather than "setting a precedent" of marking a reduction in Israel's annual package.
Albright has called the plan a "fund for Middle East peace and security."
A U.S. official said it was preferable to give Jordan money from Israel's aid package because it could be difficult to ask Congress to give more money to the Kingdom.
Jordan received $47 million in U.S. civilian and military aid this year and President Bill Clinton has asked for $75.6 million for 1998.
